npcs.name: Ragioniere Nicolò "Arrotonda" Bruzzone
npcs.title: Teller at the savings bank

lines: No more lire. I keep counting them in my sleep anyway. Nineteen thirty-six, twenty-seven. Nineteen thirty-six, twenty-seven.
{name}! Good morning. Or is it? The rate hasn't moved. It never moves. It's fixed. That's the worst part: there's nothing to worry about, so I worry about that.
Up you go! I'll wait here. I'll count. Somebody has to.
Down to the bank, under the arcades. Mind the steps. There are a lot of them. I know exactly how many.
You must be the Geometra! Bruzzone, Ragioniere, savings bank of Tonnarella. I've been on this platform since the 7:40. You came on the 10:05. I counted the trains.

sleepy: Mmm, no, not that. Mmm, one thousand nine hundred and thirty-six. Zzz

topics.label: What's the rate again?
lines: One euro, one thousand nine hundred and thirty-six lire and twenty-seven cents. Of a lira. Cents of a lira! Nobody has seen a cent of a lira since 1947.
So I round. I have to round. And every time I round, somebody in the queue says 'Arrotonda!' like I've stolen their grandmother's teeth.

topics.label: Why won't you climb the steps?
lines: One hundred and twelve, to your flat. Ninety-four from the square to the castle. Sixty-one from the arcades to the square. I don't climb them. I count them. It's different.
When the lift worked, I rode with Agostino every day. Thirty-one seconds, top to bottom. I miss those thirty-one seconds.

topics.label: Why do they call you Arrotonda?
lines: Because of the rounding. Because I give them 51 cents where it should be 51.6. I didn't make the rule. Brussels made the rule. Brussels doesn't stand in the queue.

gifts.line: A slice of focaccia. Rosetta gives me the corner bits, out of pity. Have one. Pity is very filling.
The plans of the enamel sign over the bank door. A bank needs a sign. People need to know where to be angry.

npcs.name: Fanalista Gerolamo "Lanternin" Repetto
npcs.title: Keeper of the lighthouse

lines: She's turning, {name}. Every eleven seconds, two white flashes. You can set your heart by her. I do.
I walked to Rosetta's this morning. Walked! Forty years I rowed in for focaccia. The gulls followed me anyway. Old habits.
Ahoy there. You crossed the gap? Nobody crosses the gap. Not even the gulls, and they cheat.

sleepy: Steady, old girl, two flashes, steady. Zzz

topics.label: Tell me about the light
lines: A lens from 1911, made in Paris, carried up the stair in pieces by my grandfather. Two white flashes every eleven seconds. Every ship from here to Corsica knows her voice.
Since the storm she's been dark. I still go up every evening and talk to her. She doesn't answer. Neither did my wife, and we were married fifty years.

topics.label: What happened in the storm?
lines: February. A libeccio like a wall. It took the middle out of the breakwater, the panes out of the lantern and the power out of everything.
I stayed. The keeper stays. That's the whole job, really: staying.

topics.label: The gulls follow you?
lines: Every morning, to the bakery and back. I think they believe I'm their mother. I've never corrected them. It would be rude.

gifts.line: Mussels off my rock. Steam them with a glass of white. Not for the mussels: for you.
The plans of a little lantern for a railing. Not as good as mine. Nothing is. But it helps.

npcs.name: Comandante Lorenzo "Mugugno" Traverso
npcs.title: Harbour master

lines: The Navy wrote again. No buoy. I've framed it next to the first one. Now I have two letters to grumble at. Life is rich.
The breakwater holds. I inspected it. Twice. I found nothing to complain about, which is very upsetting.
Geometra. The wind is from the north, the sea is rough, the Navy is silent and the gulls are in charge. A normal day.
You're the Geometra? About time. I wrote to Toriano in February. It's not February any more. I noticed.

sleepy: Mmm, dear Admiral, with respect, no. Zzz

topics.label: Why do they call you Mugugno?
lines: The mugugno is a Genoese sailor's right to grumble. It was written into the contracts: you could pay a sailor less, but then he was allowed to complain.
I've never taken the pay cut. I complain for free. It's a public service.

topics.label: What's the Navy's letter?
lines: If the lighthouse isn't lit by spring, they'll switch it off for good and put a buoy in the bay. A buoy! A plastic thing with a battery.
I've framed the letter on my wall so I can grumble at it every morning. It keeps me young.

topics.label: Can I take stone from the castle?
lines: The castle is a protected monument. I want that on record. Now: take the fallen bits. The sea's already taken the rest, and it never asked.

gifts.line: Farinata. Rosetta's. She burns the edges for me, the way my mother did. Don't tell her I said so. Don't tell anyone.
The plans of a proper stone block. The old breakwater was made of them. They lasted ninety years. Plastic buoys last eleven.

npcs.name: Rosetta "la Sveglia" Canepa
npcs.title: Baker of focaccia

lines: Every lira in town came through my till that night. I've never been so rich in a currency that doesn't exist.
Morning, {name}! The focaccia's out, the gulls are circling, and I've been up since four. So the usual.
You're new! Have a bit of focaccia. Quick, before. Oh. Too late. That gull. That one. We've met.

sleepy: Mmm, the dough's rising, so am I, no, I'm not. Zzz

topics.label: Why la Sveglia?
lines: My shutter goes up at four in the morning. Bang. Rattle. The whole street wakes. They used to complain. Now they set their watches by it.

topics.label: What's the trouble with the gulls?
lines: They're organised. One distracts you at the door, the other goes for the tray. I've seen them do it to a docker with a whole slice. He didn't even feel it.
Gerolamo feeds them. On purpose. I've told him. He says they're family.

topics.label: What makes good focaccia?
lines: Olive oil, salt, and fingers. You press holes all over it with your fingers, and the oil goes in the holes. My nonna said: if it doesn't shine, it isn't focaccia.
And you dunk it in milky coffee at five in the morning. People from Toriano look at you like you've done a crime.

gifts.line: Onion focaccia, from the corner of the tray. The corner's the best bit. Don't tell the dockers.
The plans of the tables outside my door. Copy them. Every street should have somewhere to sit and eat focaccia badly.

npcs.name: Giobatta "Baciccia" Parodi
npcs.title: Fishmonger at the market

lines: Don't say it. Don't say anything. Look at the frame instead. That's my last thousand-lire note. Maria Montessori. She deserved better.
Fresh bream! Mullet! Octopus that winked at me! Prices in lire, euros if you insist, and I'll sigh.
Lire. I take lire. I give change in lire. I'll be buried with lire in my pockets, and the ferryman can do the conversion.

sleepy: Mmm, three thousand a kilo, no, I won't round it. Zzz

topics.label: Why won't you take euros?
lines: I take them. I don't like them. They're too small. A thousand-lire note, you could wrap a sardine in it. A euro, you lose it in your apron.
And the prices! Two thousand lire for mussels. In euros it's one euro and three cents. One euro and three cents! It sounds like a bus ticket, not a dinner.

topics.label: What happened to your stall?
lines: The storm took the roof off and put it in the harbour. I sell off the boxes now, under the sky, like a pirate.
The fish don't mind. The customers mind. The rain minds most of all.

gifts.line: Mussels. No charge. Don't tell anyone, or I'll have to give everybody mussels, and then where would I be? Poor, with mussels.
The plans of a market counter. Marble top, so the fish stay cold. Well, it says marble. Use what you've got.

lines: I went down to the harbour today! In the lift! Agostino held the door and pretended not to cry. I pretended not to see.
{name}, you're too thin. Are you eating? Rosetta's focaccia doesn't count, it's mostly air and oil.
Ah, the Geometra. Come here, let me look at you. Too thin. You need pesto. Everybody needs pesto.

topics.label: How do you find the euro?
lines: I don't find it. It finds me, and I convert it. One euro is nearly two thousand lire. In 1955 two thousand lire was a week's shopping. So a euro is a week's shopping. So a coffee costs a week's shopping. You see? Robbery.

topics.label: What's the basket on the rope for?
lines: Everything. Bread comes up, rubbish goes down, gossip goes both ways. Before the storm I'd go down in the lift and fetch it myself.
Since the lift stopped, my knees and the stairs have had a disagreement. The stairs are winning.

topics.label: Your balcony is all basil!
lines: Forty-one pots. Genoese basil, the small leaves. The secret is: you talk to it. Not nicely. Basil likes to be told off.

gifts.line: Spring greens pie. My recipe. Rosetta says it's hers. It's mine. She was six when I taught her.
The plans for a flower bed. Put basil in it. Put basil in everything.

npcs.name: Agostino "Su e Giù" Ottonello
npcs.title: Attendant of the public lift

lines: Going down? Going up? Either way, mind the doors. Thirty-one seconds, top to bottom. I've timed it eleven thousand times.
Good morning. The lift is out of service. I am not. I'm here every day, in case it changes its mind.

sleepy: Mmm, doors closing, going down. Zzz

topics.label: How long have you run the lift?
lines: Thirty years in March. Before me, my uncle. Before him, a man called Bacigalupo who wore a top hat. There's a photo.
Everybody rides with me, so I hear everything. Who's courting, who's owing, who's selling the boat. I never repeat it. I just remember it, very loudly, in my head.

topics.label: Could the wind run it?
lines: The tramontana blows on the bastion three days out of four. My uncle always said: one day someone will put a windmill up there and we'll never pay the electric again. Nobody listened. Uncle was a great one for windmills.

gifts.line: Farinata from Rosetta's, still warm. I used to bring Nonna Pina a slice every morning, in the lift. Take it, before I get sentimental.
The plans of the bench by the top stop. Thirty years I've sat on it. It knows me better than my doctor.

npcs.name: Padron Stefano "Lampara" Dellepiane
npcs.title: Skipper of the night boat

lines: We went out under the beam last night. Six boats, six lamps, and the light going round over us like a big slow clock. Best catch since the storm.
Evening, Geometra. Or morning. On a night boat they're the same thing, with coffee in between.
No lighthouse, no fishing. You don't take a boat out past the point in the dark without the light. Not twice.

sleepy: Mmm, more to port, the lamp, the lamp. Zzz

topics.label: What's a lampara?
lines: A big lamp on a pole over the side. You go out on a dark night, no moon, and switch it on. The anchovies come up to look. They're curious. Like tourists.
Then you close the net round them, gently. They don't even notice. Also like tourists.

topics.label: Why does the lighthouse matter?
lines: There's a reef off the point they call the Bishop. It's had nine boats in my lifetime. The light keeps you off him. Without it, I stay in, and the anchovies laugh at me.

gifts.line: Anchovies, salted last spring. Eat them on focaccia, with a cold glass of something. Then thank me.
The plans of the railing on my boat. Keeps the crew on board. Mostly.

lines: The lift works! I put the scooter in it. Agostino said no. I said it's a passenger. He said it's a scooter. We're still discussing it.
Yo, Geometra. Uncle's out the back. Need anything? Rope, wire, glass, tiles? I'll find it. Probably.
Cool helmet, right? I wear it everywhere. The stairs are dangerous. Mostly because I carry the scooter up them.

topics.label: Why carry a scooter up stairs?
lines: Deliveries! Rope to the boats, glass to the lighthouse, tiles to the roofs. Half of Tonnarella is stairs. The other half is the sea. I'm working on the sea.

topics.label: Where's your uncle?
lines: Out the back. He's always out the back. I've worked here two years and I've seen him four times. I think he's in a card game that started in 1988.

topics.label: What are you listening to?
lines: A tape my cousin made off the radio. Every song has the DJ talking over the start. I know all the DJ's bits by heart. They're my favourite part.

gifts.line: Copper wire, off the end of a reel. Uncle won't notice. Uncle doesn't notice anything. He's out the back.
Plans for a streetlight, from a box in the back. Uncle had them. I think. Somebody had them.
